page: Microsoft Azure D2as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AMD EPYC 7763 processor, executing on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The configuration provides 2 dedicated vCPUs spanning a single physical core with two threads running at a base clock of 3.525 GHz. Memory capacity is 8.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance contains no dedicated local disk storage and includes no integrated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate adequate single-threaded compute relative to its resource footprint. In single-core tests, the instance records a stress-ng score of 2700.18 (placing in the top 25%) and a Geekbench single-core score of 1483.0. Single-threaded gzip compression reaches 25.96 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression reaches 11.36 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core metrics remain limited by the low core count, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 1818.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 3141.22.

Memory throughput is modest, reporting 32.41 GB/sec for uncached 256MB read operations and 22.32 GB/sec for uncached writes, yielding a PassMark memory score of 1129.21. Application-level tests reflect lower throughput overall, with Redis operations clocking 2.06 million operations per second and static web serving throughput measured at 2.57 GB/sec. On lightweight language model processing using a 135M model, the system registers 128.99 prompt tokens per second and 73.24 text generation tokens per second.

Cost efficiency is aligned with entry-level general-purpose deployments where full-system throughput is secondary to predictable single-thread responsiveness. Because local storage is not bundled, all persistent file workflows necessitate external remote block storage. Microsoft Azure D2as_v5 is best suited for low-traffic web applications, lightweight microservices, development and testing environments, and modest background utility workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure D2as_v5 is an entry-level general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core, 8.0 GB of RAM, and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor using the x86_64 instruction set. The instance lacks bundled local storage and has no GPU acceleration, requiring networked storage volumes for persistent data. Benchmark metrics reflect solid single-core responsiveness—demonstrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 1483.0 and strong stress-ng single-core output—contrasted with low aggregate multi-core and memory subsystem bandwidth due to its compact dual-vCPU footprint. Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation, the D2as_v5 is technically suited for light web serving, microservices, testing environments, and utility workloads with modest computational demands.
og_description: Microsoft Azure D2as_v5 offers 2 vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 7763 processor, 8.0 GB RAM, and Hyper-V virtualization. It delivers solid single-core performance for light web and general tasks.
